39 A nucleus of magnesium decays into a nucleus of sodium by emitting a β+ particle. The decay is
represented by the equation shown.
Mg
23
12
→  Na
P
Q
+
β
+
0
1
What are the values of P and Q?
P
Q
A
22
11

hints: Look at the top numbers in $^{23}_{12}\text{Mg} \rightarrow ^{P}_{Q}\text{Na} + ^{0}_{+1}\beta$: the top number is the nucleon number and the $\beta^+$ has top number $0$.
Now look at the bottom numbers: the bottom number is the proton number and the $\beta^+$ has bottom number $+1$, so the totals on both sides must balance.
Set up two conservation equations: $23 = P + 0$ for the top and $12 = Q + 1$ for the bottom, then solve for $P$ and $Q$.
walkthrough: Identify the notation: for $^{23}_{12}\text{Mg}$, the upper $23$ is the nucleon number $A$ and the lower $12$ is the proton number $Z$.
Recall the conservation rules in nuclear decay: total nucleon number is conserved and total proton number - charge - is conserved.
Apply nucleon-number conservation: $23 = P + 0$ because the $\beta^+$ particle $^{0}_{+1}\beta$ carries $0$ nucleons.
So $P = 23$, which means the mass number is unchanged, as expected for beta decay.
Apply proton-number conservation: $12 = Q + (+1)$ because the $\beta^+$ carries charge $+1$.
Rearrange to $Q = 12 - 1 = 11$, which shows a proton in the nucleus has changed into a neutron.
P = 23 and Q = 11 matches the row with P = 23, Q = 11. This is option C.

A.explanation: P = 22 would mean the nucleon number decreased by 1, but the $\beta^+$ particle has nucleon number $0$ so $P$ must stay at $23$.

B.explanation: P = 22 and Q = 13 do not conserve nucleon number or proton number when $^{0}_{+1}\beta$ is added to the right-hand side.

C.explanation: P = 23 conserves nucleon number and Q = 11 conserves proton number, since $23 = P + 0$ and $12 = Q + 1$.

D.explanation: Q = 13 would increase the proton number, but emission of a $+1$ charge in $\beta^+$ decay must decrease the daughter proton number by 1.
